title: What the page and GitHub rely on

entities.title: GET /auth/me
entities.summary: How the page tells a server from a plain file, and who is signed in.
guarantees: Answers JSON with configured: false when sign-in is not set up.
Otherwise configured: true and user: { login, avatar } for a valid session, or user: null.
entities.compatibility: The page treats anything but a JSON answer with configured: true as no server, so a field may be added; configured and user keep their meaning.

entities.title: /api/github/<path>
entities.summary: GitHub's REST API under the Worker's own address, for the allowed reads.
consumers: index.html (the github adapter, githubApi and ghGet)
guarantees: For a signed-in reader, GET on user, user/repos, repos/<owner>/<repo>, its git/trees/<ref> and its contents/<path> answers as api.github.com would for that reader, query string included.
Accept: application/vnd.github.raw is passed on, so a file can be read raw.
x-ratelimit-remaining and x-ratelimit-reset are passed on.
401 means no session, or a session GitHub no longer accepts.
entities.compatibility: A path the page starts using must be added to ALLOWED in the same change.

entities.title: The sign-in routes and their answers
entities.summary: How the page starts a sign-in and learns how it went.
consumers: index.html (signInUrl, showSignIn and the start of the script)
The GitHub OAuth App, whose registered callback is this route
guarantees: GET /auth/github/start takes return, a path in the app, and private=1 to ask for private repositories.
A sign-in ends at the return path, or with ?signin=denied when the reader cancelled at GitHub, or at /?signin=failed.
POST /auth/sign-out from the app's origin signs out.
entities.compatibility: Moving the callback means registering the new address on the OAuth App first.
